mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for three consecutive weeks with an accelerating slope (-0.4, -10.3, -5.8 points). This momentum reflects entrenched reduced consumer mobility that will persist absent a reversing shock, pulling the next 4-week mean below the last 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -39.9 to -56.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next 4-week mean exceeds its last 4-week mean despite the observed negative momentum, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen each week (18.1 -> 23.3), indicating growing stay-at-home behavior. If this weekly increase exceeds 2 points for two consecutive weeks, it signals a behavioral shift toward home-based living that suppresses discretionary outings and drives RETAIL_REC lower over the following 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL increases by more than 2 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 18.1 to 21.7 to 23.3 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL keeps rising at this pace but RETAIL_REC's next 2-week mean is higher than the prior 2-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous steep declines in WORKPLACES (-31.1 to -45.6) and TRANSIT (-67.1 to -75.6) are consistent with a regime of renewed restrictions on movement. In such a regime, policy constraints on non-essential travel continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declined every week in the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed or fall further yet RETAIL_REC's next 4-week mean rises above the last 4-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT decline together in the same week, the loss of commute-linked incidental trips (lunch stops, errands near transit hubs) compounds beyond either series acting alone, producing a disproportionately larger drop in RETAIL_REC over the following 2 weeks than either series individually predicts.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 6.0 points and TRANSIT fell 2.2 points in the most recent week while RETAIL_REC fell 5.8 points
failure_condition: If joint WORKPLACES/TRANSIT declines occur but RETAIL_REC's drop over the next 2 weeks is no larger than predicted by either single series alone, the interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is volatile but recently partially rebounded (-52.3 to -43.3). If PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week, it signals residents substituting outdoor leisure for indoor retail/recreation trips in the very near term, causing RETAIL_REC to dip further over the next week before any broader recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -52.3 to -43.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: If PARKS rises sharply but RETAIL_REC's next 1-week mean does not fall relative to the current week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-to-late August typically brings seasonal back-to-school and pre-autumn shopping activity that historically boosts retail footfall regardless of short-term mobility trends, partially offsetting the recent decline and lifting RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean relative to the prior period.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2020-08-15, within the seasonal back-to-school shopping window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next 4-week mean remains below the last 4-week mean despite the seasonal window, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has declined more mildly than RETAIL_REC (-13.0 to -24.1 vs -39.9 to -56.4), reflecting essential-vs-nonessential differentiation under current restrictions. If GROCERY_PHARM's weekly decline accelerates past 8 points, it signals restrictions are broadening to essential services too, implying further RETAIL_REC suppression over the next 2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell 5.7 and 4.7 points in the last two weeks respectively
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM declines sharply but RETAIL_REC's next 2-week mean rises relative to the last 2-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL combined with falling TRANSIT jointly reinforce a stay-at-home behavioral pattern: reduced transit use removes the means to reach retail/recreation venues while increased residential time reflects reduced external activity preference, together driving a deeper decline in RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks than either trend predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 18.1 to 23.3 while TRANSIT fell from -67.1 to -75.6 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues rising and TRANSIT continues falling together but RETAIL_REC's next 4-week mean is not lower than the last 4-week mean, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
